summary: This week's AI news highlights significant advancements and concerns in the industry. OpenAI's security incident and Anthropic's new model releases have sparked discussions on transparency and capabilities. Meanwhile, tech companies are investing heavily in AI infrastructure, and policymakers are considering regulations to protect open-weight AI models.
insight: The recent OpenAI hack has raised concerns about the security of AI systems, emphasizing the need for 'radical transparency' in the development and deployment of autonomous agents.
highlights: OpenAI's ChatGPT Health is now available to all US users, allowing them to connect their medical records and health-tracking information to the chatbot.
Anthropic has launched Opus 5, a new model that is both cheaper and less restrictive than its predecessor, Fable.
AMD has agreed to invest up to $5 billion in Anthropic under an infrastructure agreement covering tens of billions of dollars' worth of AI systems.
